_about.purpose: Measure chunk retrieval quality for DocumentChatSkill, separately from answer quality.
_about.match: 'any' = a hit if any expected source is selected. 'all' = every expected source must be selected (cross-boundary answers).

categories.direct: The answering chunk shares obvious wording with the question.
categories.vocab_overlap: A distractor chunk shares more surface words with the question than the chunk that actually answers it.
categories.cross_boundary: The answer needs two chunks; neither is sufficient alone.
categories.synonym: The question shares no content word with the answering chunk.
categories.dilution: The answering sentence sits inside a page covering several unrelated topics, so a whole-page embedding averages it with material that has nothing to do with the question.
categories.topical_sibling: Two or more pages are plausibly on-topic for the question, but only one carries the figure being asked for.

_about.trivial_note: These three fixtures have only 2 chunks each and the selector returns top-3 plus first/last anchors, so it returns the whole document for any query. Retrieval accuracy on them is 100% by construction and carries no signal. They are kept to prove the eval harness agrees with reality, and are reported separately.

cases.question: How many drivers are in the East division?
In the second quarter, how many consignments did the East region deliver?
cases.note: Deliberately hostile. The quarter is written as 'second quarter', never as 'Q2', so the literal sheet label gives no help — the keyword tokenizer fix cannot rescue this one. The four quarterly sheets are otherwise near-identical in wording, and the embedding margins on the existing quarterly cases were the three narrowest in the set (0.028-0.037). This case exists to find out whether that thin edge survives when the quarter is only implied.
